security_audit.summary: Most repeated findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, JSON Schema URI strings, and generated tool documentation. Confirmed risks remain in the stdio subprocess path, unpinned npx package execution, predictable /tmp PID files, and shared browser context behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @playwright/mcp to a reviewed version and document the upgrade process.
Remove --stdio or parse the command into an argv list and use shell=False.
Use mktemp or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, validate PID ownership, and quote all PID file reads.
Offer an isolated-context mode and warn users before reusing authenticated sessions.
Replace pkill pattern matching with tracked child process shutdown.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill starts Playwright MCP with npx @playwright/mcp@latest. This executes a network-fetched package version that can change without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both locations invoke the latest package directly. This is clear supply-chain risk, although it points to an official package name.

semantic_findings.title: Shared Browser Context Retains Session State
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires shared browser context across calls. This can preserve cookies and authenticated state between tasks, increasing data exposure risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require shared browser context, and the script enables it. Risk depends on user account state and task trust.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Playwright Code Execution in Browser Context
semantic_findings.description: The browser_run_code tool accepts Playwright JavaScript functions. Untrusted prompts could drive page actions or extract visible page data through the browser.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly describes a code-bearing Playwright function. It affects browser context rather than operating-system code execution.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Playwright MCP
content.value_statement: Browser tasks can take time and require repeatable steps. This skill connects Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to Playwright MCP for navigation, forms, screenshots, and extraction.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops a local Playwright MCP server with helper scripts.
Calls Playwright browser tools through a bundled MCP client.
Navigates pages, moves backward, captures snapshots, and takes screenshots.
Clicks elements, types text, fills forms, and selects dropdown options.
Runs Playwright JavaScript snippets for multi-step browser workflows.
Emits MCP tool schemas as Markdown or JSON for reference.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npx, Python 3, and Playwright browser dependencies.
Uses a local server and does not host browser automation remotely.
Shared browser context can retain cookies and session state between actions.
Browser actions depend on page accessibility snapshots and stable element refs.

use_cases.title: Check Web Flows
use_cases.description: QA engineers can automate login, form, and confirmation paths before filing defects.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Researchers can capture snapshots and screenshots while reviewing public pages.

use_cases.title: Operate Internal Tools
use_cases.description: Support teams can repeat browser steps in approved admin tools with clear commands.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Playwright MCP server, open https://example.com, take a snapshot, and summarize the visible page.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target form, get a snapshot, fill the listed fields by ref, submit it, and capture the confirmation screen.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Page Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the page, inspect the snapshot, run a safe browser evaluation to extract visible table data, and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser_run_code for an approved multi-step workflow, return the final page title, and take a screenshot of the outcome.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture visible details.
output: Started the local Playwright MCP server.
Captured the page snapshot and screenshot.
Summarized product title, price, and availability.

output_examples.input: Submit a test contact form and verify confirmation.
output: Loaded the form page and captured element refs.
Filled approved test values into the fields.
Submitted the form and waited for confirmation text.
Saved a screenshot of the final state.

output_examples.input: Review a table on a public page.
output: Opened the page and inspected the accessible snapshot.
Extracted visible row labels and values.
Returned a concise summary of the table contents.

best_practices: Use snapshots before clicks so element refs match the current page.
Stop the MCP server when browser work is complete.
Use isolated browser profiles for sensitive accounts or private data.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser_run_code from untrusted instructions.
Do not keep a shared browser context open after sensitive sessions.
Do not submit forms or make purchases without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls a local Playwright browser through MCP and can navigate to user-approved websites.

faq.question: Does it require a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper starts Playwright MCP on localhost before commands call browser tools.

faq.question: Can it fill forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can type, select options, and submit forms when element refs are available.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture viewport or full-page screenshots through Playwright MCP.

faq.question: Can it use existing browser sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The shared browser context can reuse state, so sensitive sessions need care.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted pages?
faq.answer: Use caution. Browser automation can expose page data, cookies, and form inputs to the active task.
